heading: INT. DEEP-SPACE ICE HARVESTER, CARGO BAY - NIGHT CYCLE

units.text: INT. DEEP-SPACE ICE HARVESTER, CARGO BAY - NIGHT CYCLE
A hold full of frosted cylinders.
Cold blue light.
A walkway runs between stacked ice cores.
Red alert strobes at the far door.
A TECHNICIAN (30s, coveralls, tool belt, a cracked visor) crouches at an open panel, wiring fizzing against her gloves.
Hovering above her, held in place by a bracket on the ceiling, is a pale maintenance drone with a single lens.
A speaker grille glows beneath.
Hold the light still.
units.name: TECHNICIAN

units.text: I am holding it still. You are shaking.
units.name: DRONE

units.text: The cold's doing that.
units.name: TECHNICIAN

units.text: The cold is minus four. Your hands shook at minus eleven yesterday.
units.name: DRONE

units.text: Don't narrate me.
units.name: TECHNICIAN

units.text: Then stop giving me things to narrate.
units.name: DRONE

units.text: She slams the panel shut.
Sparks fly, and the strobe goes dark.
Okay. Okay. We have twenty minutes of heat, the reactor's venting on the wrong side, and the captain's gone.
units.name: TECHNICIAN

units.text: The captain is not gone. The captain is in the airlock.
units.name: DRONE

units.text: In the airlock is gone, Winnow.
units.name: TECHNICIAN

units.text: You named me.
units.name: DRONE

units.text: I didn't name you.
units.name: TECHNICIAN

units.text: You just said Winnow.
units.name: DRONE

units.text: She stops with her hand on a cylinder.
The drone's lens irises open and closes.
It's what Dad called the little one on his ship.
units.name: TECHNICIAN

units.text: Then my name is Winnow.
units.name: DRONE

units.text: I'm Paloma.
units.name: TECHNICIAN

units.text: I know.
units.name: DRONE

units.text: Of course you do.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: The technician, PALOMA, sags against the cylinder.
The drone drifts down from the bracket, its tiny rotors blurring, and hangs at her eye level.
Paloma. I can reroute the heat but the cost is the cargo.
units.name: WINNOW

units.text: How much cargo?
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: All of it. Every core. Three years of ice.
units.name: WINNOW

units.text: We'd have nothing to sell.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: You would have a ship.
units.name: WINNOW

units.text: And a captain.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: The captain has twenty minutes of air in the lock. I can open it if I reroute. You could pull him out. It is the only variable that buys both of you time.
units.name: WINNOW

units.text: Do it.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: It would cost the whole voyage.
units.name: WINNOW

units.text: He has a daughter. I've seen the picture.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: So have I. I was there when it was taken.
units.name: WINNOW

units.text: A long moment.
In the cold hold, only the hum of the failing reactor.
Winnow. Do it.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: Rerouting now. Run, Paloma.
units.name: WINNOW

units.text: The cylinders glow amber one by one as meltwater starts to pour down the walkway.
The drone shoots toward the far door.
The technician bolts after it, boots splashing through the new river, and as she reaches the airlock, a red light turns green.
